solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A price on back of pack for a sort of chop

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so the last letter of pack is taken

parts.note: a rate is a price charged, as in hourly rate

explanation.surface: Someone haggling over a cut of meat, paying a price on top of the pack.
explanation.definitionFit: The martial art gives its name to the karate chop, a sideways blow with the hand's edge.

clue.text: Staying good, youngster much enjoys their gentle treatment

indicators.note: good is staying inside, held between the other two pieces

parts.note: a kid is a youngster
to love something is to enjoy it very much

explanation.surface: A well-behaved child who loves being handled gently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'their' is a link word pointing the treatment back to the child; kid gloves are soft goatskin gloves.
explanation.definitionFit: To handle someone with kid gloves is an idiom for treating them with great tact and delicacy.

clue.text: Soldier Santa's always seen with

definitions.meaning: a British infantryman of old, named for the scarlet uniform
Father Christmas is always pictured wearing a scarlet coat

explanation.surface: A soldier who never leaves Father Christmas's side.
explanation.definitionFit: Historic British soldiers wore scarlet tunics, and Santa is always shown in scarlet outerwear.

clue.text: As singer, be very apprehensive to miss mass

indicators.note: to miss something is to leave it out, so mass is dropped from the word

parts.note: to tremble is to shake with fear or nerves
M is the physics abbreviation for mass

explanation.surface: A nervous chorister too anxious to attend Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' is a link word; the definition is just 'singer'.
explanation.definitionFit: A treble is a boy soprano, a high-voiced choirboy.

clue.text: Dog rolling over in the morning, apparently dead?

indicators.note: turning over end to end, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, marks morning hours
a stiff is slang for a corpse, and stiff describes a body that looks lifeless

explanation.surface: A dog lying belly-up in the morning so still it seems dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolling over' turns AM into MA.
explanation.definitionFit: The mastiff is a large, powerful breed of guard dog.

clue.text: Here's Augusta, one wearing hair long and shaggy

indicators.note: the hair is worn around the one, so I goes inside

parts.note: a mane is a long, thick growth of hair, like a lion's
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Augusta pictured as a woman wearing long, untidy hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Augusta' looks like a woman's name; it is the state capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Augusta is the capital city of this US state in New England.

clue.text: Man famously put to death because upping taxes once

indicators.note: in a down clue, upping means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: cos is informal shorthand for because
rates were the local property taxes in Britain before the council tax

explanation.surface: A man executed for raising taxes long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upping' turns COS into SOC. RATES were British local property taxes, replaced in 1990.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian philosopher was condemned and made to drink hemlock in 399 BC.

clue.text: Nothing Darwin worked out could be summarised

indicators.note: worked out suggests the letters being reworked into a new order

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Darwin's theory of evolution resists any summary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked out' rearranges O and DARWIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to give a very brief summary of something, meaning briefly or in short.

clue.text: Handbill offering solution for cleaning received by father

indicators.note: the father takes the solution in, so it sits inside

parts.note: FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
lye is an alkaline solution used for washing and cleaning

explanation.surface: A leaflet advertising a cleaning fluid, handed to a priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A flyer is a small printed advertisement handed out or posted, the same as a handbill.

clue.text: Locked up by policeman, resubmit access code

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the hidden letters are read from bottom to top
the letters are locked inside these words, held in from both sides

explanation.surface: A detainee arrested by an officer and told to resubmit a password.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading 'policeman, resubmit' backwards gives the answer inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A login identity is one part of the credentials needed to get into a computer system.

clue.text: Wheeze, but get round

definitions.meaning: a wheeze is a crafty scheme or trick

explanation.surface: Someone breathless trying to get round a course.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means a cunning trick; as a verb, to evade or avoid.

clue.text: Start to wake up, mad keen to get out

parts.note: to stir is to begin to move after sleep
crazy means mad

explanation.surface: Someone just waking who is desperate to get out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start to wake up' looks like a first-letter instruction; it means STIR. STIR is also slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Being driven wild by long confinement, a prisoner becomes frantic for release.

clue.text: Ladies spread round lake to appear important

parts.note: the ladies is a women's lavatory, a loo

indicators.note: the spread goes round the lake, so L sits inside

parts.note: marge is short for margarine, a spread
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Women spreading out around a lake to seem impressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ladies' means a women's lavatory here, not women; 'spread' is margarine, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that looms large seems significant or threatening, appearing bigger in importance.

clue.text: Grieve no end after a secret affair

indicators.note: the grieving word comes after the a
the last letter of the word for grieve is dropped

parts.note: to mourn is to grieve

explanation.surface: Someone grieving endlessly after a hidden love affair ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' cuts MOURN to MOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: The French loan word for love is used in English for a love affair, especially an illicit one.

clue.text: Don't allow surgeon to take lead in operation

parts.note: a vet is an animal surgeon

indicators.note: the letter that leads in is the first one of operation

explanation.surface: A refusal to let a surgeon head the operation.
explanation.definitionFit: To veto something is to forbid it or block it with an official refusal.

clue.text: 'Unsentimental' had her dead wrong

indicators.note: wrong suggests letters in a wrong order needing rearrangement

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted remark wrongly calling a woman dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard-headed person is practical and realistic, not swayed by emotion.

clue.text: Just like an animal, to grab any spare food here

parts.note: doggy means like a dog, an animal
to bag something is to seize it

explanation.surface: Grabbing leftovers greedily, just like an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A container in which a diner takes home uneaten food from a restaurant, supposedly for the dog.

clue.text: Wild song marks birthday at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and muddled, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A rowdy song celebrating a birthday aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges M and BIRTHDAY.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece this was a frenzied choral hymn to Dionysus, hence any wildly enthusiastic song or speech.

clue.text: Fictional character given line aimed offensively at one

parts.note: a persona is a character in a play or novel, as in dramatis personae

explanation.surface: A novelist's character given a line that insults someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarks that get personal attack an individual rather than an issue.

clue.text: Man securing English gem set first in ancient ring

indicators.note: the gem is placed at the front of the rest

parts.note: a precious stone is a gem

indicators.note: the man holds English inside

parts.note: he stands for a man, the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A jeweller securing an English gem into a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' suggests jewellery after 'gem set', but the ring is one of standing stones.
explanation.definitionFit: The prehistoric monument on Salisbury Plain is a circle of standing megaliths.

clue.text: Water additive gives off sulphur more regularly

indicators.note: giving off something means letting it go, so sulphur leaves the word

parts.note: a softener is added to hard water to remove minerals
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: A chemical in the water supply releasing a sulphur smell more often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives off' looks like an emission; it removes S.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the comparative of often, meaning with greater frequency.

clue.text: To kill flies is heartless hard work

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter, here removed

parts.note: sweat is slang for hard, laborious work

explanation.surface: Killing flies is a cruel, tiring business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the middle E out of SWEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To swat is to strike an insect with a sharp blow, as with a fly swatter.

clue.text: Avert conflict with the same two forces

parts.note: war is armed conflict
do is short for ditto, meaning the same
F is the abbreviation for force, so two of them give FF

explanation.surface: Preventing a war by sending in two forces.
explanation.walkthrough: DO, short for ditto, means the same again.
explanation.definitionFit: To ward something off is to fend it off or prevent it, which is to avert it.

clue.text: One tying knot in jacket

definitions.meaning: a sailor reefing a sail ties a reef knot
a short, thick double-breasted jacket worn by sailors

explanation.surface: Someone tying a knot in their jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: It names one who reefs sails with a reef knot, and also a sailor's close-fitting jacket.

clue.text: Shall we say we are Europeans?

indicators.note: say signals that the words are to be heard rather than read

parts.note: let's is the suggestion form of shall we

explanation.surface: A hesitant suggestion that we declare ourselves European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we are' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives of Latvia, a Baltic state, are known as Latvians or by this older ethnic name.

clue.text: Credulously accept what makes a friend?

parts.note: read as an instruction, the answer's first word written upwards in a down clue spells pal, a friend

explanation.surface: Wondering what it takes to make a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: 'what makes' asks which instruction produces 'a friend'. LAP, put UP in a down light, reads PAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To swallow praise or a story eagerly and uncritically, as a cat drinks milk.

clue.text: Suffer, home closing years too soon

indicators.note: the home closes around years, enclosing them

parts.note: a pad is slang for one's home
early means before the expected time

explanation.surface: Someone shutting up their home too soon and regretting it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closing' puts Y inside PAD.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay dearly is an idiom for suffering heavily as a consequence of something.

clue.text: Beat heavily in place of confinement

definitions.meaning: to hammer with repeated heavy blows
an enclosure for stray dogs or impounded cars

explanation.surface: Someone beaten up in a prison cell.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means strike repeatedly; the noun is an enclosure where strays or vehicles are held.

clue.text: Writer, endlessly narrow-minded, in Korea, for one

parts.note: a pen is something that writes

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: insular means narrow in outlook, like an island cut off

explanation.surface: A bigoted author living in Korea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops R from INSULAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Korea juts out from the Asian mainland surrounded on three sides by sea.

clue.text: Market places once filled with large plants

indicators.note: the market places take large inside them

parts.note: fora is the Latin plural of forum, a Roman marketplace
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Old markets stocked with big pot plants.
explanation.definitionFit: The collective term for the plant life of a region, as fauna is for animals.

clue.text: Part in yearly drama at first promisingly released

parts.note: PA, per annum, means yearly
a role is a part in a play

indicators.note: the first letter of drama is taken

explanation.surface: An actor in an annual production released early for good behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: PA is per annum.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner let out on parole is freed early on a promise of good behaviour.

clue.text: Not yet marvellous housing?

parts.note: pre means before, so not yet
fab is slang for fabulous, marvellous

explanation.surface: Housing that is not yet marvellous.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the housing is a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Factory-built homes put up quickly after the Second World War were a common form of British housing.
